green.style: Elves into Bears into Beasts, trading on the ground and holding attacks until the board favors it. Giant Growth goes to blockers or to push damage in bursts - one night game double-Growthed a single attacker for an 8-point swing.
green.good: Patient combat: blocks to trade up against BR's Juzam and Robots' Su-Chi, deploys around removal, and wins long grinds (3/4 in the night corpus).
green.mistakes: Still loses the flyer race to Lion-dib-bolt - Serendibs go over the top while its board stares. No air answer is structural.

red.style: Post-burn-science allocation is visible: bolts kill early blockers and mana elves, then switch to face once its own board sticks. Curves orcs into ogres into giants.
red.good: Sequencing vs Green Growth: bolt the elf, bolt the blocker, race with orcs (won 17t). Beat Counter Flyer by making them counter cheap threats.
red.mistakes: Folds to Robots' bigger artifacts - chip attacks into Su-Chi boards with no way through.

blue.style: The format's control pillar: islands, counters held for real threats, then Air Elementals in pairs closing over four turns. Turn-1 Ancestral/Mox starts when drawn.
blue.good: Counter discipline unchanged across eras - the Moat Mill and Burn wins never dipped below 12 life. Braingeyser refills mid-game.
blue.mistakes: Lost to White Weenie: five one-drop threats outran twelve counters - width beats one-for-one answers. It needed to deploy blockers earlier instead of holding everything.

white.style: Moats early, Millstones late, wins only where the lock actually locks (ground creature decks).
white.good: The RU Aggro win is the blueprint: Moat on 7, mill from 19, never below 13.
white.mistakes: Observable waste: it stacks redundant Moats (five in one BR game) because its hand holds nothing else - harmless but a tell. Fliers, Burn, and value decks (BR's Hypnotics, Robots) simply ignore the plan: 1/4 and the format's worst seat every era.

ru.style: Flying Men tempo with bolts as interaction; Hill Giants as the top end.
ru.good: Beat Moat Mill with a 23-turn flyer grind - Flying Men over Moat is its cleanest line.
ru.mistakes: Weakest night seat (1/4): loses the artifact matchups and gets outsized by green. Its bolts went to face in the Robots loss while Su-Chi hit for four a turn - the race-read class again.

lotus.style: Mulligans to the kill, executes turn 2-3 with exact X=20s. 4/4 on the night, 89% in the gate.
lotus.good: Kill math remains perfect; it even Disintegrated a blocking Lions mid-combo when the line needed the path clear.
lotus.mistakes: The X=0 self-Disintegrate tic persists when flooded (2 of 4 games) - a wasted card that never costs the win, still on the books as the tie-band leak.

burn.style: Face, face, face - with the occasional blocker kill vs Lion-dib-bolt where the board matters. Note Handcrafted now pilots this deck at ~58% after the allocation fix, so SPZ's edge here has narrowed.
burn.good: The BR win: ten turns, every bolt to the face, exactly lethal through Juzam pressure.
burn.mistakes: Lost the burn-mirror-esque races vs Counter Flyer's flyers and Lion-dib-bolt when its own clock was slower - the deck has no second gear.

uwr.style: Vise early, Serendibs and Serras in the air, burn as reach, Disenchants on the format's artifacts. The most complete deck in the metagame.
uwr.good: The Robots win is a clinic: Sol Ring start, Disenchant the Su-Chi enabler, double Psionic Blast reach, Vise squeezing all game. Factory beats fill every idle turn.
uwr.mistakes: Lost to Burn in 8 turns after a slow draw - it can be under-defended against pure face damage when its own clock hasn't started.

robots.style: Explosive artifact starts (City into double Mox into Sage turn 1), Su-Chi pressure, and genuinely deep toolbox lines: Copy Artifact was seen copying its own Su-Chi for a second 4/4, and Armageddon landed exactly when its rocks outnumbered the opponent's lands.
robots.good: The Creatures & Bolts win: turn-5 Su-Chi copy, turn-7 Armageddon with board advantage, dead on turn 9. Mind Twist and Library close value games.
robots.mistakes: The RU loss shows the old pattern faintly - value-engine turns (Wheel, Sage, Braingeyser) while Flying Men chipped it down. Counter-respect remains the open class.

ww.style: One-drops into Crusade into Armageddon - the classic plan, and it executes: the Counter Flyer win cast Crusade turn 14 and Armageddon turn 18 with the better board, locking blue out of the game.
ww.good: Chaos Orb used as clean removal (cast then crack on a Juzam); Swords timed on real threats with the lifegain accepted knowingly.
ww.mistakes: Free mulligans produced a five-mull dig against Lotus Combo - desperate but rational in an unwinnable matchup. Loses to Robots when Su-Chi outsizes the whole team and the Factories block forever.

br.style: Demonic Tutor early for the right threat, Juzam and Hypnotic as the clock, burn clearing the way. Dark Ritual now casts only when it powers something out (the dead-ritual prune shipped this morning).
br.good: The White Weenie win: tutor turn 3, Ancestral, double Juzam by turn 9, Strip Mine on their only white source mid-attack. Hypnotic pairs strip hands while beating down.
br.mistakes: The Green loss was a mana-flood grind where its removal ran dry against sixteen creatures; Burn simply outraced it (Juzam's self-ping is real in that matchup - it dealt 4 of the 20 itself).
